answer: Identity slots are scarce licences: the ledger mints fixed seats each epoch, each holder posts a self-assessed price, pays tax on it, and anyone may buy the seat at that price. History rides on the seat, so a farm of a thousand clones must declare a thousand prices and pay tax forever; price them near zero and a rival buys the seats, inheriting the work. That perpetual tax, unlike a refundable bond, is the sybil cost. A zephyr pays only for the wind it rides; a sold seat passes its vine of reputation to the buyer; on bare karst a licence that must be priced cannot be cloned free.
